question: When we talk about 'nutrient quality' in a meal, what are we really looking at?

options.A: The physical weight of the food on the plate
options.B: The total number of calories in a meal
options.C: How well the body absorbs and uses food compounds
options.D: How long the food item can be stored safely

explanation: You've got this! Nutrient quality is all about how effectively your body can actually use what you eat, rather than just counting empty calories. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h1)

question: Why is just counting calories often not enough when caring for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Calories change drastically depending on the time of day a meal is served
options.B: Calories do not reflect whether the body can actually absorb and use the nutrients
options.C: Patient metabolism makes calorie tracking completely impossible in a hospital
options.D: Processed foods always have lower calorie counts than raw food items

explanation: Great thinking! A meal can be packed with calories yet lack the vital building blocks our cells and tissues need to heal. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h1)

question: What makes a protein source 'complete' in our diet?

options.A: It requires no digestion in the stomach
options.B: It comes exclusively from plant-based foods
options.C: It has zero saturated fat content
options.D: It contains all nine essential amino acids

explanation: Spot on! Complete proteins deliver every single essential amino acid that our bodies cannot make on their own. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: A patient with high blood pressure and high blood sugar is told to switch from white bread to whole grain bread. Why is this a great choice?

options.A: Refined white bread has no calories for the body to process
options.B: Whole grains retain fiber, which slows digestion and prevents sharp sugar spikes
options.C: Whole grains eliminate all fats from the patient's daily diet
options.D: Whole grains contain complete proteins that repair damaged blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! The natural fiber in whole grains slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping levels nice and steady. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: What does the term 'bioavailability' mean when studying nutrition?

options.A: The expiration date stamped on a packaged food item
options.B: The speed at which bacteria break down food in the large intestine
options.C: The fraction of an ingested nutrient that enters the bloodstream and becomes active
options.D: The total percentage of water found inside a raw vegetable

explanation: Exactly right! Bioavailability simply means how much of the nutrient successfully makes it past your gut and into your bloodstream to go to work. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: Why might you suggest a patient eating plant-based iron (like beans or greens) drink a glass of orange juice with their meal?

options.A: Orange juice contains phytates that bind extra minerals
options.B: Citrus acid coats the stomach lining to prevent cramping
options.C: The sugar in the juice speeds up overall stomach emptying
options.D: Vitamin C in the juice enhances the absorption of plant-based iron

explanation: Brilliant! Vitamin C gives plant iron a chemical makeover that makes it way easier for your gut to absorb. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: Which type of vitamin is most easily washed away or destroyed by long storage and boiling water?
explanation: You got it! Vitamins like C and the B-complex group love water, meaning they easily dissolve into cooking water and break down with heat. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of steaming veggies instead of boiling them in lots of water?

options.A: It prevents valuable water-soluble vitamins from leaching out into the cooking water
options.B: It stops the food from ever spoiling during long hospital storage
options.C: It doubles the amount of protein found in leafy green vegetables
options.D: It completely eliminates all natural plant sugars from the food

explanation: Spot on! Steaming uses just a little steam, locking those precious vitamins safely inside the food instead of pouring them down the sink. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: How is it possible for a patient to be overweight and still suffer from malnutrition?

options.A: Their diet may provide plenty of calories but lack essential micronutrients and protein quality
options.B: Processed foods completely block the stomach from processing any liquids
options.C: Their body refuses to store any energy as fat when they eat processed foods
options.D: Malnutrition only occurs in individuals with extremely low body mass index

explanation: Think of this as 'hidden hunger'—eating plenty of calorie-dense, low-nutrient food means getting heavy calories without the vitamins your body needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h5)

question: A surgical patient has a wound that is healing very slowly, even though they are eating enough daily calories. What is the most likely dietary culprit?

options.A: Excessive consumption of raw dietary fiber from fresh vegetables
options.B: Too many omega-3 fatty acids reducing the body's baseline temperature
options.C: Inadequate intake of high-quality protein and essential micronutrients
options.D: Drinking too much water instead of sweetened hospital beverages

explanation: Well done! Closing wounds and fighting off infection takes specific amino acids and vitamins. Without them, healing naturally slows down. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h5)

question: What does the term 'nutrient density' really mean for healthy eating?

options.A: Consuming meals that contain only fat and carbohydrate sources
options.B: Choosing foods with the longest possible shelf-life in the pantry
options.C: Getting the highest amount of vitamins and minerals per calorie of food
options.D: Eating foods that weigh as much as possible to fill the stomach

explanation: You're doing great! Nutrient density is all about getting the most nutritional bang for your buck—maximum vitamins with a sensible calorie count. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)

question: What is a simple, practical habit to ensure a patient gets a wide variety of helpful antioxidants and plant nutrients?

options.A: Eating a colorful variety of different fruits and vegetables every day
options.B: Eating the exact same single vegetable for every meal to track intake
options.C: Choosing only white and beige foods because they digest more easily
options.D: Relying entirely on multi-vitamin pills while avoiding fresh produce

explanation: Spot on! Different plant colors mean different health-boosting compounds, so eating a rainbow is always the best prescription. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)
